brief: The read rent has moved from the worker to the MANAGER, and the previous loop died of exactly this — $5.45 -> $13.72 an iteration with no gain in output, because every pass re-read a growing pile of its own memory. The worker's side is now bounded, measured and clean (45.1/46 KB at this pass; row.quota rc:0 on #167, #168 and #169). The manager's side is not bounded at all. stall.mjs's own table, slope over #149 -> #169: LEDGER-archive.md 676.4 KB +1.95 KB/iter, RUNLOG.jsonl 191.8 KB +1.13, MANAGER-LOG.md 81.6 KB +0.48, state.json 38.9 KB and falling since #167 pruned it — 988.8 KB, all four opened WHOLE on every manager pass. Bound the three that grow, by ROTATION and never by deletion: #167's `rotate-ledger.mjs --prune-only` already rolls closedCues past 40 into `closed-cues-archive.jsonl` by array position, so the shape exists — give LEDGER-archive.md, RUNLOG.jsonl and MANAGER-LOG.md the same treatment past a stated N, and make stall.mjs's memory quota read what a MANAGER opens beside what a worker does, so a breach on that side is a signal rather than a paragraph in a log nobody re-reads.
successLooksLike: `stall.mjs --report` prints a manager-side quota next to the worker's, and the four files a manager opens are bounded by a rule the table states. Every archived byte is still on disk and findable — count them before and after and show the totals match.
avoid: courtyard.html must come out byte-identical; census PASS all six groups. Do NOT change a cap while measuring against it — changing a cap mid-pass is how a loop stops noticing. Do not delete anything: rotation only. Pin any 'before' control to a REF, not to HEAD (#167's surprise).
